\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ನಟ} (naṭa)}{ನಟ (naṭa)}]{\kn{ನಟ} (naṭa) — an actor}

\label{lesson:KA-C305-nata}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for an artist, then the Kannada for a singer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ನಟ}}
\textbf{\kn{ನಟ}} — \emph{naṭa} — \textquotedblleft{}an actor\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ನಟ}} (\emph{naṭa}) is Sanskrit \emph{naṭa}, \textquotedblleft{}dancer, actor\textquotedblright{}, taken over whole as a learned loan, a tatsama (CDIAL 6933). CDIAL 6933 thinks the Sanskrit word itself probably came from a Middle Indo-Aryan form. DEDR 2936 has a Kannada \emph{naṭike}, \textquotedblleft{}the cracking of joints\textquotedblright{}, but that is a different word.
\end{cousinweb}
